title: THE ROAD THAT CUT A COUNTRY THIN AS PAPER
deck: The only road out of a flooding valley runs through a country as thin as paper, whose people have only ever met humans as sudden walls. Illuminara cannot perceive their plane, so she asks its speaker what a whole person would look like, and lies down across the road to show her.
shape: Seven scenes across eleven days: a cold line on a road, a conversation in frost, a governor's one night, a body read slice by slice, a table proved on a rolling truck and a neighbour's terms, the arithmetic of nine days, and the last crossing.

scenes.title: The Cold Line
paragraphs: *Orrin Cut, kilometre 14 · twelve days before the crest, 05:40*

The road ran through the Cut like thread through a needle, and halfway along it the air changed. Illuminara felt it before she saw the survey flags: a line of cold across the tarmac, straight as a ruled edge. Fog on the upslope side stopped at it. On the downslope side the dawn was only dawn.

Four road crew had walked into it since the autumn rains. One had lost feeling down his left side for a week. A gauge nailed to a post read minus six on the line and eleven above zero a pace either way.
Ilse Brandvold, the survey lead, had slept in her truck. She pointed at a steel plate bolted flat to the road, a metre square, white with rime.

**Ilse**  
Six weeks of geophone logs. Every ninety minutes it pulls back for about fourteen minutes, then comes down again. I thought it was groundwater. Then I put the plate on the line to measure the frost, and the frost wrote back.
Marks were forming on the rime as they watched, thin and deliberate, as if someone were breathing them there.

**Ilse**  
I have eleven hundred of those. I understand perhaps forty. The speaker is called Vesh. It's a country, Illuminara. Sheaf, it calls itself: a sheet no thicker than a coin, and the Cut goes straight through the middle of it.

**Illuminara**  
And the governor?

**Ilse**  
Opens the road at noon. Nine thousand buses and trucks, six days, no stopping. The river crests in twelve. I can't put a country on his desk. I have a steel plate and a cold spot.

Illuminara crouched and laid her palm on the rime. It burned, and under the burn she felt something she had no word for, like being looked at from the side. *I can hold a lane open,* she thought. *The lane is not the problem. I can't perceive what she can't show him, and I won't pretend to.*

scenes.title: What the Frost Said
paragraphs: *The plate on the line · twelve days before the crest, 07:10*
Vesh's words came a few strokes at a time. Ilse read them out in her flat survey voice, and Illuminara answered to the plate itself, because it seemed rude to answer to anyone else.

**Vesh**  
You are weather to us. A wall rises where there was a street, grows, narrows, is gone. Nothing is behind it. Ninety-three of us have stood inside the rising. Eleven streets are cut in two and do not rejoin.

**Illuminara**  
I'm sorry. I'm also here to ask something of you, and I would rather you heard it from me than discovered it. Nine thousand vehicles must pass in twelve days, or two hundred thousand people are under the river. I don't yet know how to pass them without cutting more of you.

**Vesh**  
You ask patience of a people whose houses you halve with every wheel. Tell me when I am allowed to be afraid.
Illuminara did not answer at once. *A reasonable question,* she thought. *A true one.*

**Illuminara**  
Now. You're allowed now. Tell me exactly what you're afraid of, so I stop guessing.

**Vesh**  
That we are not seen. A blade has no one behind it. We have never met one of you. We have met the parts of you the road lets through.

It landed in her slowly. To Sheaf a person was not a person at all. A foot was a ring that appeared, swelled and shrank. A bus was a wall. No one in that country had ever watched a thing for long enough to call it a thing.

**Illuminara**  
Show me what a wall is. Where does it start, and where does it stop?

**Vesh**  
Your road crosses us in one band, forty of your metres deep. Whatever you drive through the band is a wall in the band, as wide as the thing, for as long as it stays. If the band is full, the wall cuts a street across. In a closing the band is emptied: stalls shut, lamps out, everyone withdrawn to either side. Then a wall cuts nothing.
Ilse turned a page of her notebook and drew it as the frost wrote: a coin standing on its edge, a road through its middle, a hatched band across the road.

**Illuminara**  
So the road isn't the danger. A full band is.

**Vesh**  
Yes. And there are always some who are late.

**Illuminara**  
What would a whole one look like to you?

**Vesh**  
Slow. A shape that stays long enough to be a shape, then another a little changed. We would read it as we read a coast.
*A coast, taken one slice at a time,* she thought, and offered the only thing she had that was not a request.

**Illuminara**  
I can lie across the road and pass through the line as slowly as you choose. You set the speed. You say stop, and I stop.
The frost took a long time to answer.

**Vesh**  
It is a danger to you. It would be a danger to us if you were wrong. Come in our sleep quarter, when the streets are empty. Come with no machine.

scenes.title: One Night
paragraphs: *Staging yard, Haldane Junction · twelve days before the crest, 11:20*

Governor Halloran Ashe stood at a map of the river with a pencil behind his ear and a driver's funeral card in his breast pocket. He had buried the man on Tuesday. He heard Ilse's whole report without once looking at his watch, which Illuminara noticed and respected.

**Governor Ashe**  
I believe you. I believe there's a country in my road. I also have two hundred thousand people between a river and a hill, and a convoy that can't idle. What do you want?

**Illuminara**  
One night and the morning after. Hold the convoy here. I'm not asking you to close the road. I'm asking for a way to run it that doesn't cut anyone.

**Governor Ashe**  
That costs days. I had six. The crest is twelve.

**Illuminara**  
It may cost three. It won't cost twelve. If I can't show you something by noon tomorrow, open it. The order is yours, not mine.

**Governor Ashe**  
And if what you show me is a creature's feelings against my people's lives?

**Illuminara**  
Then I won't stand in the road. But her streets are real, Governor. So are yours.
He took the pencil from behind his ear and wrote *noon* across the staging yard on the map, hard enough to tear the paper.

scenes.title: Slice by Slice
paragraphs: *Orrin Cut, the line · eleven days before the crest, 02:20*

She lay on her back across the centre line in a thin coat, head toward Ilse's lamp, feet toward the downslope dark. Dov Karakas, the night marshal, kept the cones. Ilse knelt at the plate with a notebook on her knee. Nothing electronic was within thirty metres. Vesh had asked for that.

**Vesh**  
A thumb's width in each of your minutes. Begin.

Illuminara dug her heels into the tarmac and slid. The cold met her toes first. It crossed them like a thread drawn tight and climbed her, one band of ice laid against her skin at a time. On the plate the frost began to write, not words now but shapes, small and closed.

**Vesh**  
A ring. It grows. Another beside it. They are joining.

**Illuminara**  
My ankles. Then a leg. Then the other.

**Vesh**  
Why does it not vanish?

**Illuminara**  
Because I'm staying.

She slid on. Her knees made two long ovals, her hips one wide one, and at the ribs a curve that swelled and fell, swelled and fell. Ilse read it out in a whisper, and Illuminara felt the line of cold cross her chest like a hand laid flat.

**Vesh**  
It moves in a rhythm. Is it failing?

**Illuminara**  
Breathing. It means I'm alive.

The shape stopped changing for a long time. Illuminara lay with the cold across her ribs and her teeth beginning to chatter, and understood with a clarity that surprised her that she was being read. A country was walking the length of her, one lamp-lit street at a time, and for the first time learning that the wall had edges.
Then Vesh asked for the hand. She lifted it a thumb's width at a time, and the frost divided the curve into five, small and astonished.

**Vesh**  
You are not a blade. You are long. You have parts.

**Illuminara**  
So do you, I think.

The cold crossed her hair at 03:46. The frost drew a last round shape, and the whole of her was a drawing. At 03:49 the line melted off the plate and off the road all at once, the way a held breath is let go.

**Vesh**  
The market is closing. The streets are empty. Look.

The frost drew it for them: lanes of lamps going dark in order, doors shutting, a square emptying like a bath. Fourteen minutes of nothing. Illuminara, who had never been shown a country's evening, lay on wet tarmac and watched it breathe.

scenes.title: The Calendar
paragraphs: *The line · eleven days before the crest, 05:12*
Ilse had a sealed envelope in her breast pocket. She had written it at nine the previous evening from six weeks of geophone logs and nothing Vesh had told her, and had given it to Dov to hold.

**Ilse**  
If the logs are a calendar, it goes quiet at five-seventeen for fourteen minutes, give or take three. So eleven at the shortest. And the closing you saw at three-forty-nine was two minutes off my card. That's the part I got wrong.

**Dov**  
Two minutes is a good miss.

**Illuminara**  
Why two?
Ilse asked the plate. The frost answered quickly.

**Vesh**  
Our market runs with the river. It lags a little each cycle. Tell your surveyor to keep a table, not a constant.
Ilse wrote *table, not constant* in the margin of her envelope. At 05:18 the line melted off the road, one minute after her card. Nothing moved. Dov's thumb stayed on the radio.

**Vesh**  
Wait. Late ones are still leaving the band.
The plate stayed blank for a minute that felt like six. At 05:19 it wrote one word, small and square. *Empty.*

They sent an empty flatbed across by remote at fifteen kilometres an hour, with a second flatbed rolling up behind it. Vesh's report was on the plate before the first truck cleared the line. *No street cut. A wall passed. Nothing was in it.*

The frost came back at 05:29, a white line creeping across the tarmac from the plate outward. Ilse looked at her watch. Eleven minutes, the very bottom of her range, and the second flatbed was a length from the line, rolling on the card's promise of two more.

**Vesh**  
Market reopens. Stop.

**Dov**  
That's a red light I can read.
Dov dropped the gate. The flatbed halted a metre short of the line, and nobody argued with a strip of frost.

**Illuminara**  
And if it had been inside?

**Vesh**  
A wall through the stalls at the hour they are raised. Brass Street, fourteen stalls. We would have counted them.

Ilse wrote *eleven* under *table, not constant* and circled it twice. Illuminara watched the gate and thought of what the governor needed to hear. *Sheaf can stop us, and does, and we can see it happen.* Then she thought of the other thing, which was harder.

**Illuminara**  
Vesh, whose word would I be carrying to him? I don't want to speak for Sheaf. I want the governor to hear Sheaf.

**Vesh**  
I speak for the market, because the market is the part of us that meets your road. For the eleven cut streets I carry. I do not decide. Wait.
The plate stayed white until 09:40. Then it wrote at length, and Ilse read it aloud twice before she trusted her voice.

**Vesh**  
The streets have spoken. One: your trial may become a convoy. One lane, never the sleep quarter, never the lane over Brass Street. The first day is a trial, and if a street is cut it ends. Two: we strike a warning three of your minutes before we reopen, and we keep it even when it costs the market its early stalls. We will write you each morning the day's closings. Three: we say stop when we choose, and you do not ask why. Four: when your people have gone, the road rests seventy days while the cut streets knit. Five: if the road is ever widened, there is a seat for us, and the answer in it is ours. Six: the ninety-three go where your laws are kept, in our script.
Ilse read it back to the plate, line by line, and Vesh corrected one word.

**Vesh**  
Not a courtesy. A warning. Write warning.
She wrote it.

scenes.title: Nine Days
paragraphs: *Staging yard, Haldane Junction · eleven days before the crest, 11:50*
She put the arithmetic on the governor's table because he had asked for arithmetic and nothing else, and beside it Ilse laid the plate's transcript, Sheaf's six lines in Ilse's hand.

**Illuminara**  
Those aren't mine. Sheaf wrote them, Ilse read them back, and Vesh corrected one word. You sign them or you don't.
Ashe read the six lines slowly, the way a man reads a contract he intends to be held to.

**Governor Ashe**  
Eleven minutes. You told me fourteen last night.

**Ilse**  
Fourteen is the middle. At five-twenty-nine we watched the bottom, with a truck rolling.

**Illuminara**  
So we plan on the bottom. Eleven, less one for the band to empty and three for the warning, leaves seven to drive, at fifteen kilometres an hour. The spacing is Dov's.

**Dov**  
While we waited on the streets this morning I took the worst pair on the manifest down the approach grade: a loaded gravel tipper behind the lightest van, cold tarmac, red light dropped at fifteen. Driver's reaction counted, the tipper needed ten metres to stop. So nobody enters closer than ten metres clear of the one ahead, and the entry light holds them until they're clear. That's for a lead that vanishes. A real lead needs a few metres of its own to stop, so the margin is real.

**Illuminara**  
The manifest's mean length is ten metres, so ten clear is twenty nose to nose on average. A long vehicle waits longer, a short one less. Twelve and a half vehicles a minute, eighty-seven a pulse. Sixteen closings a day, Sheaf keeps four for sleep, twelve pulses. A thousand and forty-four a day.

**Governor Ashe**  
Nine thousand over a thousand and forty-four.

**Illuminara**  
Eight days and a bit more than half. The crest is eleven days off. Lose two pulses every day, to frost or a breakdown or a gate, and it's ten days and a third. You still clear the valley before the water.

**Governor Ashe**  
I wanted six.

**Illuminara**  
I know. Nobody is cut.
Ashe studied the table, then the frost photographs Dov had pinned beside it. For a while he said nothing.

**Governor Ashe**  
And the eleven streets already cut? I won't open a road I can be accused of lying about.

**Illuminara**  
Line four. After the evacuation the Cut closes to heavy traffic for seventy days, ambulances only, and only in a closing. They knit if nothing crosses.

**Governor Ashe**  
Seventy days. My reconstruction trucks.

**Illuminara**  
Take the river road when the water drops. Longer, I know. Ilse has costed it.

Ashe let out a long breath. Then he took the pencil and, under the order to open the road, wrote the sentence that would govern it. Convoys cross only in a pulse. The marshal follows the frost. The first day is a trial. A driver who crosses outside a pulse loses his licence for a year. Beneath it he copied Sheaf's six lines out in his own hand, so that the order would carry them as terms and not as favours.

**Governor Ashe**  
And if one of my drivers decides he's in a hurry?

**Dov**  
Then he meets me at the gate, Governor. And the gate meets him first.

scenes.title: The Ninety-Third Name
paragraphs: *The line · two days before the crest, 03:49*
The first day had been the trial. At its last pulse Vesh wrote *go on*, and the warning had struck early twenty-three times since; each time Dov dropped the gate, and each time no street was cut.

On the ninth night the last bus crossed in the first pulse after the sleep quarter, a school bus with a cracked mirror and eleven people asleep across the back seats. It went over the line at fifteen kilometres an hour, and the frost did not stir.
Nobody cheered. Dov lowered the gate, the frost came down over the road like a held cloth, and then Vesh wrote.

**Vesh**  
Nine thousand and nineteen passed. Nothing in them is cut. We will say so in the square tonight.

Then Vesh wrote the names. Ninety-three, in Sheaf's script, one to a line, and Ilse read them aloud into the dawn as the frost let them go. Governor Ashe had come out alone in his coat. He took the last name from the plate himself, halting over its vowels, and said it again to the road.

Ilse had traced the list as it came, ninety-three lines in Sheaf's own hand, and she held the sheet out to him. Ashe wrote across its head *Appendix A to the Order* and signed under the last line with the pencil from behind his ear. The clerk at the county register would stamp it at nine, he said, and file it as written, in Sheaf's script and not in a translation.

Then he handed Dov the chain. Dov ran it through the gate post and the gate and snapped the padlock, and wired a card to it in marker pen: *Heavy traffic closed. Seventy days. Day one.* One key stayed on a nail in his hut, for an ambulance in a closing. The reconstruction trucks would take the river road when the water dropped, and nobody on the line remarked that it was long.

Afterward, when the frost lay thin on the plate, a small shape grew in it, closed and round, and spread into a long one, and held. It had a head. It had two arms. Illuminara, sitting on an upturned crate with her coat around her knees, did not need it translated.

**Vesh**  
We have a picture of you now. Come again when the streets knit. Come slowly.

**Illuminara**  
I will.

critic_line: Illuminara lets a country as thin as paper read her body at its own speed, turns its fear into a shared traffic clock, and helps nine thousand and nineteen people cross before the flood while the cut streets win names in law and seventy days to heal.

shared_strengths: Strong, original premise and a moving scene where a paper-thin country learns a human is a whole person. Dialogue-rich and humane. The middle bogs down in procedural arithmetic and treaty terms, and the tidy resolution lacks real conflict. Some readers will find that slow.

A striking, lucid premise becomes an emotionally satisfying story about perception, consent, and practical compromise. The vivid slice-by-slice encounter and humane dialogue should strongly hold readers; only the extended convoy arithmetic risks briefly cooling the momentum.
shared_reservations: Eleven minutes, less one for the band to empty and three for the warning, leaves seven to drive, at fifteen kilometres an hour. The spacing is Dov's.
The manifest's mean length is ten metres, so ten clear is twenty nose to nose on average. A long vehicle waits longer, a short one less.

translation_sl.title: CESTA, KI JE PREREZALA DEŽELO, TANKO KAKOR PAPIR
translation_sl.deck: Edina cesta iz poplavljajoče doline teče skozi deželo, tanko kakor papir, katere prebivalci so ljudi vedno srečali le kot nenadne zidove. Illuminara njihove ravnine ne more zaznati, zato njihovega govorca vpraša, kako bi bil videti cel človek, in leže čez cesto, da bi mu ga pokazala.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v enajstih dneh: mrzla črta na cesti, pogovor v slani, guvernerjeva ena noč, telo, prebrano rezino za rezino, tabela, dokazana s tovornjakom v gibanju, in sosedovi pogoji, računica devetih dni ter zadnje prečkanje.

scenes.title: Mrzla črta
paragraphs: *Orrin Cut, kilometer 14 · dvanajst dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 05:40*

Cesta je tekla skozi usek kakor nit skozi šivanko, na polovici pa se je zrak spremenil. Illuminara je to začutila, preden je zagledala geodetske zastavice: črto mraza čez asfalt, ravno kakor narisan rob. Megla na strani navzgor po pobočju se je pri njej ustavila. Na spodnji strani je bila zora samo zora.

Od jesenskih nalivov so vanjo stopili štirje cestni delavci. Eden je za teden dni izgubil občutek po vsej levi strani. Merilnik, pribit na steber, je na črti kazal minus šest, korak v katero koli smer pa enajst nad ničlo.
Ilse Brandvold, vodja meritev, je spala v svojem tovornjaku. Pokazala je na jekleno ploščo, ravno privito na cesto, kvadratni meter, belo od slane.

**Ilse**  
Šest tednov zapisov geofonov. Vsakih devetdeset minut se umakne za približno štirinajst minut, nato pa se spet spusti. Mislila sem, da je podtalnica. Potem sem ploščo položila na črto, da bi izmerila slano, slana pa je odpisala.
Medtem ko so gledali, so se na slani oblikovale sledi, tanke in namerne, kakor da jih nekdo z dihom riše nanjo.

**Ilse**  
Imam jih tisoč sto. Razumem jih morda štirideset. Govorcu je ime Vesh. To je dežela, Illuminara. Imenuje se Sheaf: plošča, nič debelejša od kovanca, usek pa gre naravnost skozi njeno sredino.

**Illuminara**  
In guverner?

**Ilse**  
Opoldne odpre cesto. Devet tisoč avtobusov in tovornjakov, šest dni, brez ustavljanja. Reka doseže vrh čez dvanajst dni. Dežele mu ne morem položiti na mizo. Imam jekleno ploščo in mrzlo mesto.

Illuminara je počepnila in položila dlan na slano. Peklo jo je, pod pekočino pa je čutila nekaj, za kar ni imela besede, kakor da bi jo nekdo gledal s strani. *Vozni pas lahko držim odprt,* je pomislila. *Vozni pas ni težava. Ne morem zaznati tega, česar mu ona ne more pokazati, in ne bom se pretvarjala, da lahko.*

scenes.title: Kaj je rekla slana
paragraphs: *Plošča na črti · dvanajst dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 07:10*

Vesheve besede so prihajale po nekaj potez naenkrat. Ilse jih je brala s svojim ravnim geodetskim glasom, Illuminara pa je odgovarjala sami plošči, ker se ji je zdelo nevljudno odgovarjati komur koli drugemu.

**Vesh**  
Za nas ste vreme. Tam, kjer je bila ulica, se dvigne zid, raste, se zoži in izgine. Za njim ni ničesar. Triindevetdeset naših je stalo znotraj dviganja. Enajst ulic je prerezanih na dvoje in se ne združijo več.

**Illuminara**  
Žal mi je. Tukaj sem tudi zato, da vas nekaj prosim, in raje bi, da to slišite od mene, kakor da sami odkrijete. V dvanajstih dneh mora mimo devet tisoč vozil, sicer je dvesto tisoč ljudi pod reko. Še ne vem, kako naj jih spravim mimo, ne da bi vas še več prerezala.

**Vesh**  
Za potrpežljivost prosite ljudstvo, katerega hiše prepolovite z vsakim kolesom. Povejte mi, kdaj se smem bati.
Illuminara ni takoj odgovorila. *Razumno vprašanje,* je pomislila. *Resnično.*

**Illuminara**  
Zdaj. Zdaj se smete. Natančno mi povejte, česa se bojite, da ne bom več ugibala.

**Vesh**  
Da nas ne vidite. Za rezilom ni nikogar. Nikoli nismo srečali nikogar od vas. Srečali smo dele vas, ki jih cesta spusti skozi.

Počasi jo je zadelo. Za Sheaf človek sploh ni bil človek. Stopalo je bilo obroč, ki se je pojavil, se razširil in skrčil. Avtobus je bil zid. Nihče v tej deželi ni nikoli opazoval stvari dovolj dolgo, da bi jo lahko imenoval stvar.

**Illuminara**  
Pokažite mi, kaj je zid. Kje se začne in kje konča?

**Vesh**  
Vaša cesta nas prečka v enem pasu, globokem štirideset vaših metrov. Kar koli peljete skozi pas, je v njem zid, širok kakor stvar, dokler ostane. Če je pas poln, zid prereže ulico. Ob zaprtju se pas izprazni: stojnice se zaprejo, svetilke ugasnejo, vsi se umaknejo na eno ali drugo stran. Takrat zid ne prereže ničesar.
Ilse je obrnila stran v beležnici in narisala, kakor je pisala slana: kovanec, postavljen na rob, cesta skozi sredino, po cesti pa črtkan pas.

**Illuminara**  
Torej nevarnost ni cesta. Nevaren je poln pas.

**Vesh**  
Da. In vedno so nekateri pozni.

**Illuminara**  
Kako bi bil za vas videti cel človek?

**Vesh**  
Počasen. Oblika, ki ostane dovolj dolgo, da je oblika, nato druga, malo spremenjena. Brali bi jo, kakor beremo obalo.
*Obala, zajeta rezino za rezino,* je pomislila in ponudila edino stvar, ki jo je imela in ni bila prošnja.

**Illuminara**  
Lahko ležem čez cesto in grem skozi črto tako počasi, kakor izberete vi. Vi določite hitrost. Rečete stop in ustavim se.
Slana je dolgo molčala, preden je odgovorila.

**Vesh**  
Za vas je nevarno. Za nas bi bilo nevarno, če se motite. Pridite v času našega spanja, ko so ulice prazne. Pridite brez stroja.

scenes.title: Ena noč
paragraphs: *Zbirno dvorišče, križišče Haldane · dvanajst dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 11:20*

Guverner Halloran Ashe je stal ob zemljevidu reke s svinčnikom za ušesom in pogrebno kartico voznika v prsnem žepu. Moža je pokopal v torek. Celotno Ilsino poročilo je poslušal, ne da bi enkrat pogledal na uro, kar je Illuminara opazila in spoštovala.

**Guverner Ashe**  
Verjamem vam. Verjamem, da je na moji cesti dežela. Imam pa tudi dvesto tisoč ljudi med reko in hribom ter konvoj, ki ne more stati v prostem teku. Kaj hočete?

**Illuminara**  
Eno noč in naslednje jutro. Konvoj zadržite tukaj. Ne prosim vas, da cesto zaprete. Prosim za način vožnje, ki ne bo nikogar prerezal.

**Guverner Ashe**  
To stane dneve. Imel sem jih šest. Vrh je čez dvanajst dni.

**Illuminara**  
Morda bo stalo tri. Ne bo stalo dvanajst. Če vam do jutri opoldne ne morem česa pokazati, jo odprite. Ukaz je vaš, ne moj.

**Guverner Ashe**  
In če mi boste pokazali čustva nekega bitja proti življenjem mojih ljudi?

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne bom stala na cesti. Toda njene ulice so resnične, guverner. Tudi vaše.
Vzel je svinčnik izza ušesa in čez zbirno dvorišče na zemljevidu napisal *opoldne*, tako močno, da je raztrgal papir.

scenes.title: Rezino za rezino
paragraphs: *Orrin Cut, črta · enajst dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 02:20*

V tankem plašču je ležala na hrbtu čez sredinsko črto, z glavo proti Ilsini svetilki in nogami proti temi navzdol po pobočju. Dov Karakas, nočni nadzornik, je varoval stožce. Ilse je klečala ob plošči z beležnico na kolenu. V tridesetih metrih ni bilo ničesar elektronskega. Vesh je tako zahteval.

**Vesh**  
Za širino palca v vsaki vaši minuti. Začnite.

Illuminara je pete zarila v asfalt in zdrsnila. Mraz se je najprej dotaknil njenih prstov na nogah. Prečkal jih je kakor napeta nit in se vzpenjal po njej, pas ledu za pasom ledu ob koži. Na plošči je slana začela risati, zdaj ne besed, temveč oblike, majhne in zaprte.

**Vesh**  
Obroč. Raste. Poleg njega še eden. Združujeta se.

**Illuminara**  
Moja gležnja. Nato ena noga. Nato druga.

**Vesh**  
Zakaj ne izgine?

**Illuminara**  
Ker ostajam.

Drsela je naprej. Njeni koleni sta naredili dva dolga ovala, boki enega širokega, ob rebrih pa krivuljo, ki se je širila in spuščala, širila in spuščala. Ilse je to šepetaje brala na glas, Illuminara pa je čutila črto mraza, ki ji je prekrižala prsi kakor plosko položena dlan.

**Vesh**  
Premika se v ritmu. Ali odpoveduje?

**Illuminara**  
Dihanje. Pomeni, da sem živa.

Oblika se dolgo ni spreminjala. Illuminara je ležala z mrazom čez rebra, zobje so ji začeli šklepetati, in z jasnostjo, ki jo je presenetila, dojela, da jo berejo. Dežela je hodila po vsej njeni dolžini, eno s svetilkami osvetljeno ulico za drugo, in se prvič učila, da ima zid robove.
Nato je Vesh prosil za roko. Dvigovala jo je za širino palca naenkrat, slana pa je krivuljo razdelila na pet majhnih, začudenih delov.

**Vesh**  
Niste rezilo. Dolgi ste. Imate dele.

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da jih imate tudi vi.
Mraz je njene lase prečkal ob 03:46. Slana je narisala zadnjo okroglo obliko in vsa je postala risba. Ob 03:49 se je črta naenkrat stopila s plošče in ceste, kakor ko izpustimo zadržani dih.

**Vesh**  
Tržnica se zapira. Ulice so prazne. Poglejte.

Slana jim je to narisala: vrste svetilk, ki so ugašale po vrsti, vrata, ki so se zapirala, trg, ki se je praznil kakor kad. Štirinajst minut niča. Illuminara, ki ji še nikoli niso pokazali večera neke dežele, je ležala na mokrem asfaltu in gledala, kako diha.

scenes.title: Koledar
paragraphs: *Črta · enajst dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 05:12*
Ilse je imela v prsnem žepu zapečateno ovojnico. Prejšnji večer ob devetih jo je napisala iz šestih tednov zapisov geofonov in iz ničesar, kar ji je povedal Vesh, nato pa jo dala Dovu, da jo hrani.

**Ilse**  
Če so zapisi koledar, potihne ob petih sedemnajst za štirinajst minut, plus ali minus tri. Torej najmanj enajst. Zaprtje, ki ste ga videli ob treh devetinštirideset, pa je od moje kartice odstopalo za dve minuti. Ta del sem imela narobe.

**Dov**  
Dve minuti sta dober zgrešek.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj dve?
Ilse je vprašala ploščo. Slana je hitro odgovorila.

**Vesh**  
Naša tržnica teče z reko. Vsak cikel malo zaostane. Svoji geodetinji povejte, naj vodi tabelo, ne konstante.
Ilse je na rob ovojnice zapisala *tabela, ne konstanta*. Ob 05:18 se je črta stopila s ceste, minuto za časom na njeni kartici. Nič se ni premaknilo. Dovov palec je ostal na radijski postaji.

**Vesh**  
Počakajte. Pozni se še vedno umikajo iz pasu.
Plošča je ostala prazna minuto, ki se je zdela dolga šest minut. Ob 05:19 je napisala eno samo besedo, majhno in oglato. *Prazno.*

Čeznjo so z daljinskim upravljanjem poslali prazen tovornjak z ravno ploščadjo pri petnajstih kilometrih na uro, drugi pa je vozil za njim. Veshevo poročilo je bilo na plošči, še preden je prvi tovornjak zapustil črto. *Nobena ulica ni prerezana. Zid je šel mimo. V njem ni bilo ničesar.*

Slana se je vrnila ob 05:29, bela črta je od plošče lezla čez asfalt navzven. Ilse je pogledala na uro. Enajst minut, samo dno njenega razpona, drugi tovornjak pa je bil za dolžino oddaljen od črte in se je premikal na obljubo kartice o še dveh minutah.

**Vesh**  
Tržnica se odpira. Ustavite.

**Dov**  
To je rdeča luč, ki jo znam brati.
Dov je spustil zapornico. Tovornjak se je ustavil meter pred črto in nihče se ni prepiral s pasom slane.

**Illuminara**  
In če bi bil že v njem?

**Vesh**  
Zid skozi stojnice ob uri, ko jih postavljajo. Brass Street, štirinajst stojnic. Prešteli bi jih.

Ilse je pod *tabela, ne konstanta* zapisala *enajst* in ga dvakrat obkrožila. Illuminara je gledala zapornico in razmišljala o tem, kaj mora slišati guverner. *Sheaf nas lahko ustavi, to tudi stori in mi lahko vidimo, da se zgodi.* Nato je pomislila na drugo stvar, ki je bila težja.

**Illuminara**  
Vesh, čigavo besedo bi mu nesla? Nočem govoriti v imenu Sheaf. Hočem, da guverner sliši Sheaf.

**Vesh**  
Govorim za tržnico, ker je tržnica del nas, ki se sreča z vašo cesto. Za enajst prerezanih ulic prenašam besede. Ne odločam. Počakajte.
Plošča je ostala bela do 09:40. Nato je dolgo pisala in Ilse je besedilo dvakrat prebrala na glas, preden je zaupala svojemu glasu.

**Vesh**  
Ulice so spregovorile. Prvič: vaš poskus lahko postane konvoj. En vozni pas, nikoli v času spanja, nikoli pas čez Brass Street. Prvi dan je poskus in če se prereže ulica, se konča. Drugič: opozorimo tri vaše minute pred ponovnim odprtjem in opozorilo ohranimo tudi takrat, ko tržnico stane prvih stojnic. Vsako jutro vam bomo napisali zaprtja tistega dne. Tretjič: ko se sami odločimo, rečemo stop in vi ne vprašate zakaj. Četrtič: ko vaši ljudje odidejo, cesta počiva sedemdeset dni, medtem ko se prerezane ulice celijo. Petič: če se cesta kdaj razširi, je za nas en sedež in odgovor na njem je naš. Šestič: triindevetdeset imen gre tja, kjer hranite svoje zakone, v naši pisavi.
Ilse je plošči prebrala nazaj, vrstico za vrstico, Vesh pa je popravil eno besedo.

**Vesh**  
Ne vljudnost. Opozorilo. Napišite opozorilo.
Napisala jo je.

scenes.title: Devet dni
paragraphs: *Zbirno dvorišče, križišče Haldane · enajst dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 11:50*
Na guvernerjevo mizo je položila računico, ker je prosil za računico in nič drugega, Ilse pa je poleg nje položila prepis s plošče, šest vrstic Sheaf, prepisanih z Ilsino roko.

**Illuminara**  
Te niso moje. Napisala jih je Sheaf, Ilse jih je prebrala nazaj, Vesh pa je popravil eno besedo. Podpišete jih ali pa ne.
Ashe je šest vrstic prebral počasi, kakor človek bere pogodbo, ki naj bi veljala tudi zanj.

**Guverner Ashe**  
Enajst minut. Sinoči ste mi rekli štirinajst.

**Ilse**  
Štirinajst je sredina. Ob petih devetindvajset smo videli dno, medtem ko je vozil tovornjak.

**Illuminara**  
Torej načrtujemo po dnu. Enajst, minus ena za izpraznitev pasu in tri za opozorilo, pusti sedem za vožnjo pri petnajstih kilometrih na uro. Razmik je Dovov.

**Dov**  
Ko smo danes zjutraj čakali na ulice, sem po dovoznem klancu peljal najslabši par s seznama: naložen prekucnik gramoza za najlažjim kombijem, mrzel asfalt, rdeča luč pri petnajstih. Z upoštevanim odzivom voznika je prekucnik za ustavitev potreboval deset metrov. Zato nihče ne zapelje bliže kakor deset metrov proste poti za tistim spredaj, vstopna luč pa ga zadrži, dokler razdalja ni prosta. To velja, če vozilo spredaj izgine. Resnično vozilo spredaj potrebuje še nekaj metrov za svojo ustavitev, zato je rezerva resnična.

**Illuminara**  
Povprečna dolžina vozila na seznamu je deset metrov, zato deset metrov proste poti pomeni povprečno dvajset metrov od nosa do nosa. Dolgo vozilo čaka dlje, kratko manj. Dvanajst in pol vozila na minuto, sedeminosemdeset v enem valu. Šestnajst zaprtij na dan, štiri Sheaf obdrži za spanje, torej dvanajst valov. Tisoč štiriinštirideset na dan.

**Guverner Ashe**  
Devet tisoč deljeno s tisoč štiriinštirideset.

**Illuminara**  
Osem dni in malo več kot polovica. Vrh je oddaljen enajst dni. Vsak dan izgubite dva vala, zaradi slane ali okvare ali zapornice, in traja deset dni in tretjino. Dolino še vedno izpraznite pred vodo.

**Guverner Ashe**  
Hotel sem šest.

**Illuminara**  
Vem. Nihče ni prerezan.
Ashe je preučil tabelo, nato fotografije slane, ki jih je Dov pripel poleg nje. Nekaj časa ni rekel ničesar.

**Guverner Ashe**  
Kaj pa enajst že prerezanih ulic? Ne bom odprl ceste, zaradi katere me lahko obtožijo laži.

**Illuminara**  
Četrta vrstica. Po evakuaciji se Orrin Cut za sedemdeset dni zapre za težki promet, dovoljena so le reševalna vozila in še ta samo med zaprtjem. Če nič ne prečka, se ulice celijo.

**Guverner Ashe**  
Sedemdeset dni. Moji tovornjaki za obnovo.

**Illuminara**  
Ko voda upade, naj gredo po rečni cesti. Daljša je, vem. Ilse je izračunala stroške.

Ashe je dolgo izdihnil. Nato je vzel svinčnik in pod ukazom o odprtju ceste napisal stavek, ki jo bo urejal. Konvoji prečkajo samo v valu. Nadzornik sledi slani. Prvi dan je poskus. Voznik, ki prečka zunaj vala, za eno leto izgubi dovoljenje. Pod to je s svojo roko prepisal šest vrstic Sheaf, da bi jih ukaz nosil kot pogoje in ne kot usluge.

**Guverner Ashe**  
In če se eden od mojih voznikov odloči, da se mu mudi?

**Dov**  
Potem pri zapornici sreča mene, guverner. Zapornica pa ga sreča prva.

scenes.title: Triindevetdeseto ime
paragraphs: *Črta · dva dni pred poplavnim vrhom, 03:49*

Prvi dan je bil poskus. V zadnjem valu je Vesh napisal *nadaljujte*, opozorilo pa je od tedaj prišlo prezgodaj triindvajsetkrat; vsakič je Dov spustil zapornico in vsakič ni bila prerezana nobena ulica.

Deveto noč je zadnji avtobus prečkal v prvem valu po času spanja, šolski avtobus s počenim ogledalom in enajstimi ljudmi, ki so spali čez zadnje sedeže. Črto je prevozil pri petnajstih kilometrih na uro in slana se ni premaknila.
Nihče ni navijal. Dov je spustil zapornico, slana se je čez cesto spustila kakor pridržana tkanina, nato pa je Vesh napisal.

**Vesh**  
Mimo jih je šlo devet tisoč devetnajst. Nič v njih ni prerezano. Nocoj bomo to povedali na trgu.

Nato je Vesh napisal imena. Triindevetdeset, v pisavi Sheaf, eno v vsako vrstico, Ilse pa jih je na glas brala v zoro, ko jih je slana spuščala. Guverner Ashe je prišel sam v plašču. Zadnje ime je sam prevzel s plošče, se spotikal čez njegove samoglasnike in ga še enkrat izgovoril cesti.

Ilse je sproti prerisovala seznam, triindevetdeset vrstic z lastno roko Sheaf, in mu izročila list. Ashe je na vrh napisal *Priloga A k ukazu* in se s svinčnikom izza ušesa podpisal pod zadnjo vrstico. Uradnik v okrožnem registru ga bo žigosal ob devetih, je rekel, in ga vložil takšnega, kakor je napisan, v pisavi Sheaf in ne v prevodu.

Nato je Dovu izročil verigo. Dov jo je speljal skozi steber zapornice in zapornico ter zaprl obešanko, nato pa nanjo z žico pritrdil kartico, napisano s flomastrom: *Težki promet zaprt. Sedemdeset dni. Prvi dan.* En ključ je ostal na žeblju v njegovi uti, za reševalno vozilo med zaprtjem. Tovornjaki za obnovo bodo, ko voda upade, šli po rečni cesti in nihče na črti ni pripomnil, da je dolga.

Pozneje, ko je slana tanko ležala na plošči, je v njej zrasla majhna oblika, zaprta in okrogla, se razširila v dolgo ter obstala. Imela je glavo. Imela je dve roki. Illuminara, ki je sedela na obrnjenem zaboju s plaščem okoli kolen, ni potrebovala prevoda.

**Vesh**  
Zdaj imamo vašo sliko. Vrnite se, ko se ulice zacelijo. Pridite počasi.

**Illuminara**  
Bom.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara dovoli deželi, tanki kakor papir, da njeno telo bere s svojo hitrostjo, njen strah spremeni v skupno prometno uro in pomaga devet tisoč devetnajstim ljudem prečkati pred poplavo, medtem ko prerezane ulice dobijo imena v zakonu in sedemdeset dni za celjenje.
